This vignette walks through a network analysis with Graphical-SUBHO (Bhadury, Mitra and
Gaskins 2023, [arXiv:2308.02713](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.02713)). All data are simulated.
The sampler is shortened so that the vignette builds in seconds; use the defaults of
`subho()` for an analysis.

```{r}
library(GGMsubho)
```

## Data

`subho()` takes a numeric matrix with samples in rows and variables in columns. Here the
true network is known.

```{r}
sim <- simulate_ggm(n = 100, p = 15, structure = "random", edge_prob = 0.12,
                    node_names = sprintf("Gene%02d", 1:15), seed = 2026)
dim(sim$data)
sum(sim$graph[upper.tri(sim$graph)])
```

## Fit

Every variable is regressed on the others under a horseshoe prior. Predictors are ranked by
the size of their coefficient, and a step-up comparison of nested models selects a
neighbourhood.

```{r}
fit <- subho(sim$data, n_iter = 500, burn = 100, thin = 2, seed = 1)
fit
summary(fit, "and")
```

## The network

The AND rule keeps an edge when both nodes select each other; the OR rule when either does.

```{r}
round(graph_metrics(fit$graph_and, sim$graph), 3)
net <- network_data(fit, rule = "and")
head(net$edges)
top_connected(fit, top = 5)
```

## Figures

`plot_network()` returns a `ggplot` object. Edge colour shows the sign of the partial
correlation, edge width its magnitude, and node size the sum of absolute partial
correlations at the node.

```{r}
plot_network(fit, subtitle = "AND rule")
```

The edges can instead be coloured by groups of nodes.

```{r}
clusters <- cluster_nodes(sim$data, k = 3)
plot_network(fit, clusters = clusters)
```

## Comparing methods

The comparison methods of the article return the same kind of object, so they work with the
same tools. Here is the graphical horseshoe of Li, Craig and Bhadra (2019).

```{r}
ghs <- ghs_ggm(sim$data, burn = 100, n_save = 300, seed = 1)
ghs
round(graph_metrics(ghs$graph, sim$graph), 3)
```

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE), fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.6}
plot_network_panels(list(Truth = sim$partial_cor, SUBHO = fit, GHS = ghs), ncol = 3)
```

## References

Bhadury S, Mitra R, Gaskins JT (2023). Fast Bayesian High-Dimensional Gaussian Graphical
Model Estimation. arXiv:2308.02713.

Li Y, Craig BA, Bhadra A (2019). The graphical horseshoe estimator for inverse covariance
matrices. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 28(3), 747-757.
